description: AERPAW at North Carolina State University publishes this experimental collection. This release extends the earlier AERPAW air-to-ground campaign with four flights at 3.4 GHz, consisting of two linear and two zigzag trajectories. A fixed LW1 transmitter communicates with a receiver UAV at approximately 60 metres. DataCite describes raw SigMF signals and processed CSV and NPZ files containing positions, headings, distances and path loss. The extension has its own DOI and distinct flight scope. Coverage is limited to the described experimental campaign. The linked Dryad release is registered under CC0 1.0 and is publicly accessible without charge. Formats and variables are described by the provider; the files were not downloaded. Caveats include campaign-specific equipment and conditions, which limit transfer to other networks. Simulation use: Air-to-ground propagation and path-loss modelling. Related records include the NSF PAWR testbed platform, which describes the wider experimental infrastructure.
